# Changelog

All notable changes to bareloop are documented here. Format:
[Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/); versioning:
[SemVer](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html). Pre-1.0: **minor** = a ladder rung or
feature lands, **patch** = docs, fixes, scaffolding.

## [0.54.1] - 2026-11-04

### Fixed

- **The review door's held line no longer says a rubric green earns no learning credit.** A rubric run's lessons count at run end (PRD v1.112); only reuse/bridge credit waits for Accept, so `src/u-readout.js` now says "NO reuse credit until you accept it", and `bareloop.context.md` says the same in its two places. The same wording is fixed where Accept's release is described elsewhere: the door's Accept line (`src/u-readout.js`), the run-u HELD line (`src/userrun.js`), the `bridges.js`/`reuse.js` door comments, and the tests pinning them. Also, the learn-ledger climb test's failure message no longer quotes a time figure.
- **The step a money or time cap escalated reads capped, not failed.** A run that ended capped left its last step's card at `failed` because that step's own `step-end` says `escalated` and carries no stop reason (real spines msi0w2i5 and msx87qqs: the cap's escalation lands just before the step-end). `src/panel/server.js` now gives the run's LAST step part the cap word where the run's verdict is known, and only when that step's own escalation was the cap: a wall-halt reads time cap, a money cap-halt reads money cap (the replay part now carries its `tripped` escalation, with `ladder` when its strike limit ended it). A step its own strike limit escalated stays failed even if the run then ended on the cap (the ladder's stop is also category `cap-halt`, real spine u-mshcpdg4), and so does an earlier escalated step.
- **`climb` and `foldCards` no longer compare card pairs already in one family.** Same families, levels and groups (checked identical against the old code on 4,000 random ledgers for `climb`, and on 4,300 random and real-shaped card sets for `foldCards`); 2,000 same-lesson rows take about 60 ms instead of about 400 ms, which removes the load flake in `tests/learn-ledger.test.js`. `tests/launcher-stop-deadline.test.js` now uses a fake clock through a new optional `clock` dep of the launcher (default `performance.now`, no change for real callers), so load can no longer flip it.

## [0.54.0] - 2026-11-03

### Added

- **A worker that ends a try in text without writing is nudged once (F282).** When a writeable step's (or the fix loop's) ask finishes with text and the gate audit holds no allowed write or edit for it, the same conversation is continued once with one fixed message (`TEXT_ONLY_NUDGE`: "You ended without writing any file. Make the change now with your write or edit tool; do not reply in text."). The nudge round is inside the same try, metered like every other round, and honours the money cap, the wall clock, Stop and the round limit; read-only steps are never nudged and nothing is forced (no `toolChoice`). A new spine record `worker-text-only` stores the worker's last text (secret-masked, up to 2,000 characters, `truncated`) with `nudged` and `nudgeWrote`; the Audit marks a nudged try "nudged" in its grid header. Test-proven only; not seen live.
- **An always-on guard can cover a job line (F281).** A drafted close may list `guardLines: [{guard, lines}]` beside its stages, so a job line the mandatory guards fully do (for example "fix the cause in src/, no suppression comments") needs no duplicate stage and no refusal; the validator checks the link names a real guard and real lines, the drafter is told the guards exist and shown a legal example, and the plan card shows "check - always-on: <guard>" under the line. Specs without the field are unchanged.
- **The Audit shows the memo and the learnings where they were passed (F274).** The `carry-note` spine record now carries the memo text itself (secret-masked, up to 12,000 characters per ask), and the Audit tab shows it as a closed fold "Memory this worker got" under the part and try that received it; the learnings the planner got show as a fold on the drafting/plan part and the first replan part. The bottom "What the planner was told" box is gone (no text shown twice). Runs from before this change read "not saved (older run)". Matched by recorded phase, iteration and spine order, never by timestamp.
- **bare-agent `^0.59.0` bad-call handling (BA-29; F265, F266, F267).** The worker Loop turns on `checkArgs` (an object where a string was declared is refused before the tool runs, with the corrected hint). A new spine record `worker-bad-calls` names each bad call from bare-agent's structured `badCalls`/`cutOff` (kind, tool, param, expected, got, size, `hasAppend`, round); `worker-malformed-tool-call` is no longer lost on a round cut at the output cap. The next attempt's note says what was cut or refused (write in parts with `append`, decide sooner when reasoning dominates, send JSON as text). Test-proven only; not seen live.
- **`pairEditGrant` (F271, B2 safety net).** A plan step granting `write` without `edit` is paired with `edit` by code at the draft, replan and resume sites, only when the signed ceiling offers `edit` and never for a rubric step-file step. Internal (not exported). Test-proven, including the three live gutting plans as a fixture; not seen live.

- **BA-30 `shrinkGuard` on every worker (F272, F276).** A whole-file `write` that would cut a file tracked at the seed to under half its size (and at least 2 KB) is refused with the file unchanged, and the worker is told to use `edit`, `append:true` or `content:''`. "Tracked at seed" is the files at HEAD at the start of the leg, read from the worker tree for every job (command, declared or rubric close), compared in real-path form (a symlinked parent or root cannot launder a path); a file the worker creates later is not guarded; a resumed leg counts what earlier legs committed as tracked. The authoring scout has no write tool and takes no guard.

### Changed

- **`seedListing` reads `git ls-tree -z`** so file names with non-ASCII bytes list as themselves, not C-quoted (F276).
- **Planner and persona wording (F271, B).** `EXIT_EXAMPLE` now teaches the read-only look-around step shape (tools read, grep with an `artifact-written` exit on an existing file); the two persona lines say "the file-changing tool you were given" instead of "the write tool", a tool a look-around step does not hold. Drafter-only POC (prereg `docs/logs/PLANWORDING-PREREG.md`): a leaning, 7 drafts per arm.
- **Gate audit write/edit rows record `valueType` and UTF-8 `bytes`** (F267): an object content no longer reads as 15 bytes and non-ASCII text is no longer under-counted.
- **Plain panel words for a stuck refused-argument loop**: the Ended block names what the model did instead of "(code: interpreter-red)"; the terminal outcome is unchanged (the escalation record gains `badCall`).
- **Panel caption looks, carried from fwdloop (hamr's request).** Chat job card field captions are accent pills (no left bar); the `[n]` numbers are gone from both tab rows; field captions elsewhere (global label, Settings money labels) are 12px bold accent, with checkbox/radio labels unchanged; the Runs tab section captions are colour bars with a count pill (Needs you amber, Running now teal, Scheduled blue, Jobs grey) and a divider between Jobs cards; the Run tab ENDED/NEXT/SCHEDULE labels and the Summary and Map captions are accent bold. Not carried (no such element here): the Ask door/evidence headings, the Result grid headings (the Result tab uses boxes). Look only; checked by screenshot at desktop width, not at phone width.
- **Run summary row labels are blue bold (hamr, 2026-11-03).** The `model:`, `steps:`, `why:`, `close:`, `tools:`, `calls:`, `checks:` and `cache:` labels in the Run tab SUMMARY box wear the accent colour and bold, like ENDED / NEXT / SCHEDULE; values unchanged. Scoped to the Run summary; the Import box keeps its faint labels. Look only.
- **Chat New job card pills say what is required (hamr, 2026-11-03; fwdloop 0ae68fb pattern).** A small grey `required` sits inside the caption pill of Job name, The job, Inputs, Destination and Cap $ — the five fields `validateJobCard` refuses when empty; Model, Check type and Time cap carry none. Look only.
- **Audit tab caption words are blue (hamr, 2026-11-03; fwdloop e637bb8).** In the Audit / logs tab the table header cells (check grid, Flat table, drafting, door and rounds tables), the `errors` and `rounds per try` captions, the `try N` labels in the errors list and the row labels of the schedule and learnings tables wear the accent colour (bold where they were not already). Scoped to `#audit-body`; values, the `[ +N more lines ]` buttons and the red/green marks are unchanged. Look only.
- **Runs tab search block is a light card (hamr, 2026-11-03; fwdloop V1).** The dashed line above search is gone; the "search also finds Scheduled" note (accent bold, SEARCH caption) and the search box sit together on one tinted card with rounded corners, the box has a 1px accent border and a focus ring. CSS only. Checked by screenshot at 1280 and 390 widths (no horizontal scroll), light and dark.
- **Audit grid shows what a worker was told as a `told in this run` row, like fwdloop (hamr, 2026-11-03; fwdloop 1574dcb).** In a step's or the fix loop's check grid, a row under the header has one `[ N lines ]` button per try that was handed the carry memo and a dash for a try that was not; a click opens the exact saved text under `errors` (8 lines, then `[ +N more lines ]`), a second click closes it. This replaces the per-try "Memory this worker got" folds in grids. A run with no saved memo text (older run) draws no row. The learnings stay a fold on the planner part (the planner, not a step try, is what gets them), so there is no `told from earlier runs` row. A try outside a grid (single-attempt step, the fix loop's cut-off try) keeps the old fold.
- bare-agent pin `^0.55.0` to `^0.59.0` (clean-install peers checked: bareguard 0.27.0 deduped).

## [0.53.0] - 2026-11-02

### Added

- **EXPERIMENTAL, default off: a first-read map (`readMap`, docs/logs/MAP-PREREG.md).** With the signed spec field `readMap: true`, the first `shell_read` of a 200+ line non-test file in an ask returns a map of its named parts (`symbol start-end`, openable with `ctx_get`) instead of file bytes; the second read of that path is today's read, and the file is never marked delivered by the map. No `ctx_get` in the step's grant, no index or no named chunk: today's read plus a report-only `read-map-skip` record. One report-only `read-map` spine record per map. Absent = off and byte-identical; the switch enters the signed hash only when present. Not proven: the pre-registered battery decides. Tested 2026-10-31: FAIL, stays off (F263).

### Changed

- **The carry memo is always on: no switch (hamr 2026-11-01).** The `carryNote` key in `config.json` is retired (ignored on read, dropped on any config write), a job spec's `handoffNote` is still accepted and hashed (old signed specs verify) but has no effect, and `runJob`/`runPlan` no longer take a `carryNote` option. A live OLD-vs-NEW check of the fold on one job found no regression (F264).
- **The handoff note is folded into the carry memo.** One block (the memo's files-read lines now carry the function line ranges, dropped first at the cap) (the switch this fold left behind, `carryNote`, was removed the next day: see above); a job spec's `handoffNote` is legacy; the `handoff-note` spine record is no longer written (old spines replay unchanged).

- **Seed note ON by default, part of the carry-over memory (`seedNote`, F262, docs/logs/SEEDGAP-PREREG.md).** The planner's first draft (its own block) and, through the carry memo's "Earlier failures (folded):" section labelled `at start`, every step and fix worker are told, read-only, what the job's own `count-not-worse` check said on the untouched tree ("At start, the job's own check said:" plus that stage's text, secret-masked). Absent = on; `seedNote: false` turns it off and is byte-identical to before; the switch enters the signed hash only when present, so old signed jobs get it with no re-sign. Result: on the big-file job 3 of 3 ON runs wrote to the culprit file vs 1 of 3 OFF (n=3, one job, one patient; carry note on in all six). The battery tested planner + first worker of step 1; the shipped delivery to workers is the memo (every worker; seen live once, run u-mvwok8nk, all 4 memos carried it).

- **The carry note is bigger and says more about failures (F261).** Its cap rises from 3,000 to 12,000 characters (7 of 8 notes in a live run were capped). Each try line now says how the try ended and what its check said ("Ran out of calls (24 of 24). Its check failed."; "Check not run." when no check ran). A new "Earlier failures (folded):" section, after "Earlier tries (folded):", carries each failed check's whole text (secrets masked, kept in `state.json` so a resume has it), folded by the learnings rule with the newest member shown; the last try's failure is left out only when that try failed (its retry prompt already carries it); a failure from a try that was later passed stays. Over the cap the order is files, searches, earlier tries, earlier failures (oldest group first), then diff hunks. The `carry-note` spine record's `sections` gains a `failures` count.

### Fixed

- **The carry note no longer says an earlier try's check passed when it failed or never ran.** A try's outcome was guessed from whether the NEXT prompt carried the retry marker, so a step's last red try followed by a replan or a new step (no marker) read "Its check passed." The engine now hands the store the check result it already knows (green, red, or unknown on an instrument fault) as each try is judged; a try with no result says "No check result was recorded for it." Note shape and the OFF path are unchanged.

texts.Changelog:
# Changelog

All notable changes to bareloop are documented here. Format:
[Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/); versioning:
[SemVer](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html). Pre-1.0: **minor** = a ladder rung or
feature lands, **patch** = docs, fixes, scaffolding.

## [0.54.1] - 2026-11-04

### Fixed

- **The review door's held line no longer says a rubric green earns no learning credit.** A rubric run's lessons count at run end (PRD v1.112); only reuse/bridge credit waits for Accept, so `src/u-readout.js` now says "NO reuse credit until you accept it", and `bareloop.context.md` says the same in its two places. The same wording is fixed where Accept's release is described elsewhere: the door's Accept line (`src/u-readout.js`), the run-u HELD line (`src/userrun.js`), the `bridges.js`/`reuse.js` door comments, and the tests pinning them. Also, the learn-ledger climb test's failure message no longer quotes a time figure.
- **The step a money or time cap escalated reads capped, not failed.** A run that ended capped left its last step's card at `failed` because that step's own `step-end` says `escalated` and carries no stop reason (real spines msi0w2i5 and msx87qqs: the cap's escalation lands just before the step-end). `src/panel/server.js` now gives the run's LAST step part the cap word where the run's verdict is known, and only when that step's own escalation was the cap: a wall-halt reads time cap, a money cap-halt reads money cap (the replay part now carries its `tripped` escalation, with `ladder` when its strike limit ended it). A step its own strike limit escalated stays failed even if the run then ended on the cap (the ladder's stop is also category `cap-halt`, real spine u-mshcpdg4), and so does an earlier escalated step.
- **`climb` and `foldCards` no longer compare card pairs already in one family.** Same families, levels and groups (checked identical against the old code on 4,000 random ledgers for `climb`, and on 4,300 random and real-shaped card sets for `foldCards`); 2,000 same-lesson rows take about 60 ms instead of about 400 ms, which removes the load flake in `tests/learn-ledger.test.js`. `tests/launcher-stop-deadline.test.js` now uses a fake clock through a new optional `clock` dep of the launcher (default `performance.now`, no change for real callers), so load can no longer flip it.

## [0.54.0] - 2026-11-03

### Added

- **A worker that ends a try in text without writing is nudged once (F282).** When a writeable step's (or the fix loop's) ask finishes with text and the gate audit holds no allowed write or edit for it, the same conversation is continued once with one fixed message (`TEXT_ONLY_NUDGE`: "You ended without writing any file. Make the change now with your write or edit tool; do not reply in text."). The nudge round is inside the same try, metered like every other round, and honours the money cap, the wall clock, Stop and the round limit; read-only steps are never nudged and nothing is forced (no `toolChoice`). A new spine record `worker-text-only` stores the worker's last text (secret-masked, up to 2,000 characters, `truncated`) with `nudged` and `nudgeWrote`; the Audit marks a nudged try "nudged" in its grid header. Test-proven only; not seen live.
- **An always-on guard can cover a job line (F281).** A drafted close may list `guardLines: [{guard, lines}]` beside its stages, so a job line the mandatory guards fully do (for example "fix the cause in src/, no suppression comments") needs no duplicate stage and no refusal; the validator checks the link names a real guard and real lines, the drafter is told the guards exist and shown a legal example, and the plan card shows "check - always-on: <guard>" under the line. Specs without the field are unchanged.
- **The Audit shows the memo and the learnings where they were passed (F274).** The `carry-note` spine record now carries the memo text itself (secret-masked, up to 12,000 characters per ask), and the Audit tab shows it as a closed fold "Memory this worker got" under the part and try that received it; the learnings the planner got show as a fold on the drafting/plan part and the first replan part. The bottom "What the planner was told" box is gone (no text shown twice). Runs from before this change read "not saved (older run)". Matched by recorded phase, iteration and spine order, never by timestamp.
- **bare-agent `^0.59.0` bad-call handling (BA-29; F265, F266, F267).** The worker Loop turns on `checkArgs` (an object where a string was declared is refused before the tool runs, with the corrected hint). A new spine record `worker-bad-calls` names each bad call from bare-agent's structured `badCalls`/`cutOff` (kind, tool, param, expected, got, size, `hasAppend`, round); `worker-malformed-tool-call` is no longer lost on a round cut at the output cap. The next attempt's note says what was cut or refused (write in parts with `append`, decide sooner when reasoning dominates, send JSON as text). Test-proven only; not seen live.
- **`pairEditGrant` (F271, B2 safety net).** A plan step granting `write` without `edit` is paired with `edit` by code at the draft, replan and resume sites, only when the signed ceiling offers `edit` and never for a rubric step-file step. Internal (not exported). Test-proven, including the three live gutting plans as a fixture; not seen live.

- **BA-30 `shrinkGuard` on every worker (F272, F276).** A whole-file `write` that would cut a file tracked at the seed to under half its size (and at least 2 KB) is refused with the file unchanged, and the worker is told to use `edit`, `append:true` or `content:''`. "Tracked at seed" is the files at HEAD at the start of the leg, read from the worker tree for every job (command, declared or rubric close), compared in real-path form (a symlinked parent or root cannot launder a path); a file the worker creates later is not guarded; a resumed leg counts what earlier legs committed as tracked. The authoring scout has no write tool and takes no guard.

### Changed

- **`seedListing` reads `git ls-tree -z`** so file names with non-ASCII bytes list as themselves, not C-quoted (F276).
- **Planner and persona wording (F271, B).** `EXIT_EXAMPLE` now teaches the read-only look-around step shape (tools read, grep with an `artifact-written` exit on an existing file); the two persona lines say "the file-changing tool you were given" instead of "the write tool", a tool a look-around step does not hold. Drafter-only POC (prereg `docs/logs/PLANWORDING-PREREG.md`): a leaning, 7 drafts per arm.
- **Gate audit write/edit rows record `valueType` and UTF-8 `bytes`** (F267): an object content no longer reads as 15 bytes and non-ASCII text is no longer under-counted.
- **Plain panel words for a stuck refused-argument loop**: the Ended block names what the model did instead of "(code: interpreter-red)"; the terminal outcome is unchanged (the escalation record gains `badCall`).
- **Panel caption looks, carried from fwdloop (hamr's request).** Chat job card field captions are accent pills (no left bar); the `[n]` numbers are gone from both tab rows; field captions elsewhere (global label, Settings money labels) are 12px bold accent, with checkbox/radio labels unchanged; the Runs tab section captions are colour bars with a count pill (Needs you amber, Running now teal, Scheduled blue, Jobs grey) and a divider between Jobs cards; the Run tab ENDED/NEXT/SCHEDULE labels and the Summary and Map captions are accent bold. Not carried (no such element here): the Ask door/evidence headings, the Result grid headings (the Result tab uses boxes). Look only; checked by screenshot at desktop width, not at phone width.
- **Run summary row labels are blue bold (hamr, 2026-11-03).** The `model:`, `steps:`, `why:`, `close:`, `tools:`, `calls:`, `checks:` and `cache:` labels in the Run tab SUMMARY box wear the accent colour and bold, like ENDED / NEXT / SCHEDULE; values unchanged. Scoped to the Run summary; the Import box keeps its faint labels. Look only.
- **Chat New job card pills say what is required (hamr, 2026-11-03; fwdloop 0ae68fb pattern).** A small grey `required` sits inside the caption pill of Job name, The job, Inputs, Destination and Cap $ — the five fields `validateJobCard` refuses when empty; Model, Check type and Time cap carry none. Look only.
- **Audit tab caption words are blue (hamr, 2026-11-03; fwdloop e637bb8).** In the Audit / logs tab the table header cells (check grid, Flat table, drafting, door and rounds tables), the `errors` and `rounds per try` captions, the `try N` labels in the errors list and the row labels of the schedule and learnings tables wear the accent colour (bold where they were not already). Scoped to `#audit-body`; values, the `[ +N more lines ]` buttons and the red/green marks are unchanged. Look only.
- **Runs tab search block is a light card (hamr, 2026-11-03; fwdloop V1).** The dashed line above search is gone; the "search also finds Scheduled" note (accent bold, SEARCH caption) and the search box sit together on one tinted card with rounded corners, the box has a 1px accent border and a focus ring. CSS only. Checked by screenshot at 1280 and 390 widths (no horizontal scroll), light and dark.
- **Audit grid shows what a worker was told as a `told in this run` row, like fwdloop (hamr, 2026-11-03; fwdloop 1574dcb).** In a step's or the fix loop's check grid, a row under the header has one `[ N lines ]` button per try that was handed the carry memo and a dash for a try that was not; a click opens the exact saved text under `errors` (8 lines, then `[ +N more lines ]`), a second click closes it. This replaces the per-try "Memory this worker got" folds in grids. A run with no saved memo text (older run) draws no row. The learnings stay a fold on the planner part (the planner, not a step try, is what gets them), so there is no `told from earlier runs` row. A try outside a grid (single-attempt step, the fix loop's cut-off try) keeps the old fold.
- bare-agent pin `^0.55.0` to `^0.59.0` (clean-install peers checked: bareguard 0.27.0 deduped).

## [0.53.0] - 2026-11-02

### Added

- **EXPERIMENTAL, default off: a first-read map (`readMap`, docs/logs/MAP-PREREG.md).** With the signed spec field `readMap: true`, the first `shell_read` of a 200+ line non-test file in an ask returns a map of its named parts (`symbol start-end`, openable with `ctx_get`) instead of file bytes; the second read of that path is today's read, and the file is never marked delivered by the map. No `ctx_get` in the step's grant, no index or no named chunk: today's read plus a report-only `read-map-skip` record. One report-only `read-map` spine record per map. Absent = off and byte-identical; the switch enters the signed hash only when present. Not proven: the pre-registered battery decides. Tested 2026-10-31: FAIL, stays off (F263).

### Changed

- **The carry memo is always on: no switch (hamr 2026-11-01).** The `carryNote` key in `config.json` is retired (ignored on read, dropped on any config write), a job spec's `handoffNote` is still accepted and hashed (old signed specs verify) but has no effect, and `runJob`/`runPlan` no longer take a `carryNote` option. A live OLD-vs-NEW check of the fold on one job found no regression (F264).
- **The handoff note is folded into the carry memo.** One block (the memo's files-read lines now carry the function line ranges, dropped first at the cap) (the switch this fold left behind, `carryNote`, was removed the next day: see above); a job spec's `handoffNote` is legacy; the `handoff-note` spine record is no longer written (old spines replay unchanged).

- **Seed note ON by default, part of the carry-over memory (`seedNote`, F262, docs/logs/SEEDGAP-PREREG.md).** The planner's first draft (its own block) and, through the carry memo's "Earlier failures (folded):" section labelled `at start`, every step and fix worker are told, read-only, what the job's own `count-not-worse` check said on the untouched tree ("At start, the job's own check said:" plus that stage's text, secret-masked). Absent = on; `seedNote: false` turns it off and is byte-identical to before; the switch enters the signed hash only when present, so old signed jobs get it with no re-sign. Result: on the big-file job 3 of 3 ON runs wrote to the culprit file vs 1 of 3 OFF (n=3, one job, one patient; carry note on in all six). The battery tested planner + first worker of step 1; the shipped delivery to workers is the memo (every worker; seen live once, run u-mvwok8nk, all 4 memos carried it).

- **The carry note is bigger and says more about failures (F261).** Its cap rises from 3,000 to 12,000 characters (7 of 8 notes in a live run were capped). Each try line now says how the try ended and what its check said ("Ran out of calls (24 of 24). Its check failed."; "Check not run." when no check ran). A new "Earlier failures (folded):" section, after "Earlier tries (folded):", carries each failed check's whole text (secrets masked, kept in `state.json` so a resume has it), folded by the learnings rule with the newest member shown; the last try's failure is left out only when that try failed (its retry prompt already carries it); a failure from a try that was later passed stays. Over the cap the order is files, searches, earlier tries, earlier failures (oldest group first), then diff hunks. The `carry-note` spine record's `sections` gains a `failures` count.

### Fixed

- **The carry note no longer says an earlier try's check passed when it failed or never ran.** A try's outcome was guessed from whether the NEXT prompt carried the retry marker, so a step's last red try followed by a replan or a new step (no marker) read "Its check passed." The engine now hands the store the check result it already knows (green, red, or unknown on an instrument fault) as each try is judged; a try with no result says "No check result was recorded for it." Note shape and the OFF path are unchanged.

# Changelog

All notable changes to bareloop are documented here. Format:
[Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/); versioning:
[SemVer](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html). Pre-1.0: **minor** = a ladder rung or
feature lands, **patch** = docs, fixes, scaffolding.

## [0.54.1] - 2026-11-04

### Fixed

- **The review door's held line no longer says a rubric green earns no learning credit.** A rubric run's lessons count at run end (PRD v1.112); only reuse/bridge credit waits for Accept, so `src/u-readout.js` now says "NO reuse credit until you accept it", and `bareloop.context.md` says the same in its two places. The same wording is fixed where Accept's release is described elsewhere: the door's Accept line (`src/u-readout.js`), the run-u HELD line (`src/userrun.js`), the `bridges.js`/`reuse.js` door comments, and the tests pinning them. Also, the learn-ledger climb test's failure message no longer quotes a time figure.
- **The step a money or time cap escalated reads capped, not failed.** A run that ended capped left its last step's card at `failed` because that step's own `step-end` says `escalated` and carries no stop reason (real spines msi0w2i5 and msx87qqs: the cap's escalation lands just before the step-end). `src/panel/server.js` now gives the run's LAST step part the cap word where the run's verdict is known, and only when that step's own escalation was the cap: a wall-halt reads time cap, a money cap-halt reads money cap (the replay part now carries its `tripped` escalation, with `ladder` when its strike limit ended it). A step its own strike limit escalated stays failed even if the run then ended on the cap (the ladder's stop is also category `cap-halt`, real spine u-mshcpdg4), and so does an earlier escalated step.
- **`climb` and `foldCards` no longer compare card pairs already in one family.** Same families, levels and groups (checked identical against the old code on 4,000 random ledgers for `climb`, and on 4,300 random and real-shaped card sets for `foldCards`); 2,000 same-lesson rows take about 60 ms instead of about 400 ms, which removes the load flake in `tests/learn-ledger.test.js`. `tests/launcher-stop-deadline.test.js` now uses a fake clock through a new optional `clock` dep of the launcher (default `performance.now`, no change for real callers), so load can no longer flip it.

## [0.54.0] - 2026-11-03

### Added

- **A worker that ends a try in text without writing is nudged once (F282).** When a writeable step's (or the fix loop's) ask finishes with text and the gate audit holds no allowed write or edit for it, the same conversation is continued once with one fixed message (`TEXT_ONLY_NUDGE`: "You ended without writing any file. Make the change now with your write or edit tool; do not reply in text."). The nudge round is inside the same try, metered like every other round, and honours the money cap, the wall clock, Stop and the round limit; read-only steps are never nudged and nothing is forced (no `toolChoice`). A new spine record `worker-text-only` stores the worker's last text (secret-masked, up to 2,000 characters, `truncated`) with `nudged` and `nudgeWrote`; the Audit marks a nudged try "nudged" in its grid header. Test-proven only; not seen live.
- **An always-on guard can cover a job line (F281).** A drafted close may list `guardLines: [{guard, lines}]` beside its stages, so a job line the mandatory guards fully do (for example "fix the cause in src/, no suppression comments") needs no duplicate stage and no refusal; the validator checks the link names a real guard and real lines, the drafter is told the guards exist and shown a legal example, and the plan card shows "check - always-on: <guard>" under the line. Specs without the field are unchanged.
- **The Audit shows the memo and the learnings where they were passed (F274).** The `carry-note` spine record now carries the memo text itself (secret-masked, up to 12,000 characters per ask), and the Audit tab shows it as a closed fold "Memory this worker got" under the part and try that received it; the learnings the planner got show as a fold on the drafting/plan part and the first replan part. The bottom "What the planner was told" box is gone (no text shown twice). Runs from before this change read "not saved (older run)". Matched by recorded phase, iteration and spine order, never by timestamp.
- **bare-agent `^0.59.0` bad-call handling (BA-29; F265, F266, F267).** The worker Loop turns on `checkArgs` (an object where a string was declared is refused before the tool runs, with the corrected hint). A new spine record `worker-bad-calls` names each bad call from bare-agent's structured `badCalls`/`cutOff` (kind, tool, param, expected, got, size, `hasAppend`, round); `worker-malformed-tool-call` is no longer lost on a round cut at the output cap. The next attempt's note says what was cut or refused (write in parts with `append`, decide sooner when reasoning dominates, send JSON as text). Test-proven only; not seen live.
- **`pairEditGrant` (F271, B2 safety net).** A plan step granting `write` without `edit` is paired with `edit` by code at the draft, replan and resume sites, only when the signed ceiling offers `edit` and never for a rubric step-file step. Internal (not exported). Test-proven, including the three live gutting plans as a fixture; not seen live.

- **BA-30 `shrinkGuard` on every worker (F272, F276).** A whole-file `write` that would cut a file tracked at the seed to under half its size (and at least 2 KB) is refused with the file unchanged, and the worker is told to use `edit`, `append:true` or `content:''`. "Tracked at seed" is the files at HEAD at the start of the leg, read from the worker tree for every job (command, declared or rubric close), compared in real-path form (a symlinked parent or root cannot launder a path); a file the worker creates later is not guarded; a resumed leg counts what earlier legs committed as tracked. The authoring scout has no write tool and takes no guard.

### Changed

- **`seedListing` reads `git ls-tree -z`** so file names with non-ASCII bytes list as themselves, not C-quoted (F276).
- **Planner and persona wording (F271, B).** `EXIT_EXAMPLE` now teaches the read-only look-around step shape (tools read, grep with an `artifact-written` exit on an existing file); the two persona lines say "the file-changing tool you were given" instead of "the write tool", a tool a look-around step does not hold. Drafter-only POC (prereg `docs/logs/PLANWORDING-PREREG.md`): a leaning, 7 drafts per arm.
- **Gate audit write/edit rows record `valueType` and UTF-8 `bytes`** (F267): an object content no longer reads as 15 bytes and non-ASCII text is no longer under-counted.
- **Plain panel words for a stuck refused-argument loop**: the Ended block names what the model did instead of "(code: interpreter-red)"; the terminal outcome is unchanged (the escalation record gains `badCall`).
- **Panel caption looks, carried from fwdloop (hamr's request).** Chat job card field captions are accent pills (no left bar); the `[n]` numbers are gone from both tab rows; field captions elsewhere (global label, Settings money labels) are 12px bold accent, with checkbox/radio labels unchanged; the Runs tab section captions are colour bars with a count pill (Needs you amber, Running now teal, Scheduled blue, Jobs grey) and a divider between Jobs cards; the Run tab ENDED/NEXT/SCHEDULE labels and the Summary and Map captions are accent bold. Not carried (no such element here): the Ask door/evidence headings, the Result grid headings (the Result tab uses boxes). Look only; checked by screenshot at desktop width, not at phone width.
- **Run summary row labels are blue bold (hamr, 2026-11-03).** The `model:`, `steps:`, `why:`, `close:`, `tools:`, `calls:`, `checks:` and `cache:` labels in the Run tab SUMMARY box wear the accent colour and bold, like ENDED / NEXT / SCHEDULE; values unchanged. Scoped to the Run summary; the Import box keeps its faint labels. Look only.
- **Chat New job card pills say what is required (hamr, 2026-11-03; fwdloop 0ae68fb pattern).** A small grey `required` sits inside the caption pill of Job name, The job, Inputs, Destination and Cap $ — the five fields `validateJobCard` refuses when empty; Model, Check type and Time cap carry none. Look only.
- **Audit tab caption words are blue (hamr, 2026-11-03; fwdloop e637bb8).** In the Audit / logs tab the table header cells (check grid, Flat table, drafting, door and rounds tables), the `errors` and `rounds per try` captions, the `try N` labels in the errors list and the row labels of the schedule and learnings tables wear the accent colour (bold where they were not already). Scoped to `#audit-body`; values, the `[ +N more lines ]` buttons and the red/green marks are unchanged. Look only.
- **Runs tab search block is a light card (hamr, 2026-11-03; fwdloop V1).** The dashed line above search is gone; the "search also finds Scheduled" note (accent bold, SEARCH caption) and the search box sit together on one tinted card with rounded corners, the box has a 1px accent border and a focus ring. CSS only. Checked by screenshot at 1280 and 390 widths (no horizontal scroll), light and dark.
- **Audit grid shows what a worker was told as a `told in this run` row, like fwdloop (hamr, 2026-11-03; fwdloop 1574dcb).** In a step's or the fix loop's check grid, a row under the header has one `[ N lines ]` button per try that was handed the carry memo and a dash for a try that was not; a click opens the exact saved text under `errors` (8 lines, then `[ +N more lines ]`), a second click closes it. This replaces the per-try "Memory this worker got" folds in grids. A run with no saved memo text (older run) draws no row. The learnings stay a fold on the planner part (the planner, not a step try, is what gets them), so there is no `told from earlier runs` row. A try outside a grid (single-attempt step, the fix loop's cut-off try) keeps the old fold.
- bare-agent pin `^0.55.0` to `^0.59.0` (clean-install peers checked: bareguard 0.27.0 deduped).

## [0.53.0] - 2026-11-02

### Added

- **EXPERIMENTAL, default off: a first-read map (`readMap`, docs/logs/MAP-PREREG.md).** With the signed spec field `readMap: true`, the first `shell_read` of a 200+ line non-test file in an ask returns a map of its named parts (`symbol start-end`, openable with `ctx_get`) instead of file bytes; the second read of that path is today's read, and the file is never marked delivered by the map. No `ctx_get` in the step's grant, no index or no named chunk: today's read plus a report-only `read-map-skip` record. One report-only `read-map` spine record per map. Absent = off and byte-identical; the switch enters the signed hash only when present. Not proven: the pre-registered battery decides. Tested 2026-10-31: FAIL, stays off (F263).

### Changed

- **The carry memo is always on: no switch (hamr 2026-11-01).** The `carryNote` key in `config.json` is retired (ignored on read, dropped on any config write), a job spec's `handoffNote` is still accepted and hashed (old signed specs verify) but has no effect, and `runJob`/`runPlan` no longer take a `carryNote` option. A live OLD-vs-NEW check of the fold on one job found no regression (F264).
- **The handoff note is folded into the carry memo.** One block (the memo's files-read lines now carry the function line ranges, dropped first at the cap) (the switch this fold left behind, `carryNote`, was removed the next day: see above); a job spec's `handoffNote` is legacy; the `handoff-note` spine record is no longer written (old spines replay unchanged).

- **Seed note ON by default, part of the carry-over memory (`seedNote`, F262, docs/logs/SEEDGAP-PREREG.md).** The planner's first draft (its own block) and, through the carry memo's "Earlier failures (folded):" section labelled `at start`, every step and fix worker are told, read-only, what the job's own `count-not-worse` check said on the untouched tree ("At start, the job's own check said:" plus that stage's text, secret-masked). Absent = on; `seedNote: false` turns it off and is byte-identical to before; the switch enters the signed hash only when present, so old signed jobs get it with no re-sign. Result: on the big-file job 3 of 3 ON runs wrote to the culprit file vs 1 of 3 OFF (n=3, one job, one patient; carry note on in all six). The battery tested planner + first worker of step 1; the shipped delivery to workers is the memo (every worker; seen live once, run u-mvwok8nk, all 4 memos carried it).

- **The carry note is bigger and says more about failures (F261).** Its cap rises from 3,000 to 12,000 characters (7 of 8 notes in a live run were capped). Each try line now says how the try ended and what its check said ("Ran out of calls (24 of 24). Its check failed."; "Check not run." when no check ran). Over the cap the order is files, searches, earlier tries, earlier failures (oldest group first), then diff hunks. The `carry-note` spine record's `sections` gains a `failures` count.

### Fixed

- **The carry note no longer says an earlier try's check passed when it failed or never ran.** A try's outcome was guessed from whether the NEXT prompt carried the retry marker, so a step's last red try followed by a replan or a new step (no marker) read "Its check passed." The engine now hands the store the check result it already knows (green, red, or unknown on an instrument fault) as each try is judged; a try with no result says "No check result was recorded for it." - **The review door's held line no longer says a rubric green earns no learning credit.** A rubric run's lessons count at run end (PRD v1.112); only reuse/bridge credit waits for Accept, so `src/u-readout.js` now says "NO reuse credit until you accept it", and `bareloop.context.md` says the same in its two places. The same wording is fixed where Accept's release is described elsewhere: the door's Accept line (`src/u-readout.js`), the run-u HELD line (`src/userrun.js`), the `bridges.js`/`reuse.js` door comments, and the tests pinning them. Also, the learn-ledger climb test's failure message no longer quotes a time figure.
- **The step a money or time cap escalated reads capped, not failed.** A run that ended capped left its last step's card at `failed` because that step's own `step-end` says `escalated` and carries no stop reason (real spines msi0w2i5 and msx87qqs: the cap's escalation lands just before the step-end). `src/panel/server.js` now gives the run's LAST step part the cap word where the run's verdict is known, and only when that step's own escalation was the cap: a wall-halt reads time cap, a money cap-halt reads money cap (the replay part now carries its `tripped` escalation, with `ladder` when its strike limit ended it). A step its own strike limit escalated stays failed even if the run then ended on the cap (the ladder's stop is also category `cap-halt`, real spine u-mshcpdg4), and so does an earlier escalated step.
- **`climb` and `foldCards` no longer compare card pairs already in one family.** Same families, levels and groups (checked identical against the old code on 4,000 random ledgers for `climb`, and on 4,300 random and real-shaped card sets for `foldCards`); 2,000 same-lesson rows take about 60 ms instead of about 400 ms, which removes the load flake in `tests/learn-ledger.test.js`. `tests/launcher-stop-deadline.test.js` now uses a fake clock through a new optional `clock` dep of the launcher (default `performance.now`, no change for real callers), so load can no longer flip it.

## [0.53.0] - 2026-11-02

### Added

- **EXPERIMENTAL, default off: a first-read map (`readMap`, docs/logs/MAP-PREREG.md).** With the signed spec field `readMap: true`, the first `shell_read` of a 200+ line non-test file in an ask returns a map of its named parts (`symbol start-end`, openable with `ctx_get`) instead of file bytes; the second read of that path is today's read, and the file is never marked delivered by the map. No `ctx_get` in the step's grant, no index or no named chunk: today's read plus a report-only `read-map-skip` record. One report-only `read-map` spine record per map. Absent = off and byte-identical; the switch enters the signed hash only when present. Not proven: the pre-registered battery decides. Tested 2026-10-31: FAIL, stays off (F263).

### Changed

- **The carry memo is always on: no switch (hamr 2026-11-01).** The `carryNote` key in `config.json` is retired (ignored on read, dropped on any config write), a job spec's `handoffNote` is still accepted and hashed (old signed specs verify) but has no effect, and `runJob`/`runPlan` no longer take a `carryNote` option. A live OLD-vs-NEW check of the fold on one job found no regression (F264).
- **The handoff note is folded into the carry memo.** One block (the memo's files-read lines now carry the function line ranges, dropped first at the cap) (the switch this fold left behind, `carryNote`, was removed the next day: see above); a job spec's `handoffNote` is legacy; the `handoff-note` spine record is no longer written (old spines replay unchanged).

- **Seed note ON by default, part of the carry-over memory (`seedNote`, F262, docs/logs/SEEDGAP-PREREG.md).** The planner's first draft (its own block) and, through the carry memo's "Earlier failures (folded):" section labelled `at start`, every step and fix worker are told, read-only, what the job's own `count-not-worse` check said on the untouched tree ("At start, the job's own check said:" plus that stage's text, secret-masked). Absent = on; `seedNote: false` turns it off and is byte-identical to before; the switch enters the signed hash only when present, so old signed jobs get it with no re-sign. Result: on the big-file job 3 of 3 ON runs wrote to the culprit file vs 1 of 3 OFF (n=3, one job, one patient; carry note on in all six). The battery tested planner + first worker of step 1; the shipped delivery to workers is the memo (every worker; seen live once, run u-mvwok8nk, all 4 memos carried it).

- **The carry note is bigger and says more about failures (F261).** Its cap rises from 3,000 to 12,000 characters (7 of 8 notes in a live run were capped). Each try line now says how the try ended and what its check said ("Ran out of calls (24 of 24). Its check failed."; "Check not run." when no check ran). A new "Earlier failures (folded):" section, after "Earlier tries (folded):", carries each failed check's whole text (secrets masked, kept in `state.json` so a resume has it), folded by the learnings rule with the newest member shown; the last try's failure is left out only when that try failed (its retry prompt already carries it); a failure from a try that was later passed stays. Over the cap the order is files, searches, earlier tries, earlier failures (oldest group first), then diff hunks. The `carry-note` spine record's `sections` gains a `failures` count.

### Fixed

- **The carry note no longer says an earlier try's check passed when it failed or never ran.** A try's outcome was guessed from whether the NEXT prompt carried the retry marker, so a step's last red try followed by a replan or a new step (no marker) read "Its check passed." The engine now hands the store the check result it already knows (green, red, or unknown on an instrument fault) as each try is judged; a try with no result says "No check result was recorded for it." Note shape and the OFF path are unchanged.
